summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with end-stage liver disease from hepatitis C, hepatocellular carcinoma, and type 2 diabetes, was admitted for altered mental status and hypoglycemia. She had a blood sugar of 42 on presentation and was treated with glucagon and IV dextrose. Initial confusion was attributed to both hypoglycemia and hepatic encephalopathy, with improvement after restarting and titrating lactulose and initiating rifaximin. Brain and abdominal imaging showed no acute abnormalities, and no infection was identified. Her insulin regimen was simplified to 4 units of glargine at bedtime to prevent recurrent lows, especially given poor oral intake. She remained stable, regained baseline mental status, and was discharged home with home health services. Follow-up was arranged with primary care, hepatology, and for liver MRI.
